review_basis: semantic distinctness and Otsu4 practice value

decisions.rationale: Transport-container material requirement is a direct and previously uncovered legal proposition.
Structure/max-volume delegation is a distinct legal boundary from material selection.
Default use of prescribed transport containers is a core transport rule absent from canonical 161.
Same-site movement exception tests an independently useful exception boundary.
External name/quantity marking requirement is a separate compliance proposition.
Fall/topple/breakage prevention is an operational loading requirement distinct from marking and container rules.
Upward opening orientation is an exact, high-signal loading rule.
Sunlight/rain protection adds a distinct environmental-exposure control.
Mixed-loading restriction is a separate transport safety control.
Stacking-height ceiling is an independently testable loading boundary.
Friction/movement control addresses in-transit physical stability rather than static loading.
Vehicle placard threshold at specified quantity is a distinct quantity-triggered transport duty.
Temporary-stop safe-location rule adds a scenario-specific duty after the same quantity threshold.
Suitable onboard fire equipment is a different threshold-triggered obligation from placarding.
Leak emergency requires both mitigation and notification and is a high-value transport incident decision.

Although it reuses specified-quantity aggregation arithmetic, it applies that calculation to the Article 30 transport threshold and therefore adds a materially different legal consequence from canonical OTSU4-Q-000004.
Pre-transfer inspection of valves/caps/extinguishers is a distinct transfer-specific control.
Long-duration transfer staffing requirement is a separate personnel-safety boundary.

collision_review.note: No B10 answer-defining proposition materially duplicates canonical 161 or another Wave 3 candidate. C016 intentionally applies familiar aggregation arithmetic to a distinct transport-duty consequence.

source_review_scope: This gate checks source registration, locator reproducibility and answer-binding completeness; final canonical source verification remains separate after Permanent ID integration.
